messages:
Maria: Heads up, I started seeing a spike of NaNs coming out of attention after the recent kernel-selector rollout (v2.14). Mostly on long contexts (>4096) with BF16 on A100.
Liam: Yikes. Do you have a tiny repro or logs?
Maria: Minimal repro below — it fails reliably when ALiBi is enabled and we fall back to the ROPE-compatible kernel on long seqs.
Maria: ```python
# tiny repro
q = torch.randn(2, 32, 4096, 64, device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16)
k = torch.randn(2, 32, 4096, 64, device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16)
att = torch.einsum('b h i d, b h j d -> b h i j', q, k)
att = att * (1.0 / math.sqrt(64.0))
att = att + alibi_bias  # after this the softmax often produces NaNs
att = torch.softmax(att, dim=-1)
```
Jun: Any numeric dumps where you can see inf/NaN before softmax? That would pin it to an overflow/add issue.
Maria: I dumped stats. With BF16 I see max ~ 1e38 and min ~ -1e38 and occasional +/-inf after the bias add. In FP32 the same sequence is fine.
Ryan: That pattern points at exponent overflow in BF16. ALiBi biases grow with distance; slope * distance might exceed bf16 dynamic range for long sequences.
Sophia: Currently our ALiBi computation quantizes slopes to bf16 inside the kernel. If slope * distance overflows BF16 exponent, we end up with infs.
Liam: Quick mitigation ideas: 1) clamp bias values prior to adding, 2) compute bias and do the final add+softmax in FP32 for affected paths. Which is cheaper at scale?
Jun: Also consider keeping only bias computations in FP32, or storing per-head slopes in FP32 and expanding in FP32 before casting. KV cache in FP32 only for positional ops could be heavy.
Maria: Perf note: switching the whole attention path to FP32 increases time ~1.8x on A100 microbenchmarks. Thats too costly for broad rollout.
Ryan: Mixed precision approach seems promising: maintain most compute in BF16/FP16 but promote logits to FP32 just before bias add and softmax. Softmax numerics generally need FP32 for stability anyway.
Sophia: Another option: scale model-level ALiBi slopes so max(|slope * max_distance|) is within a safe threshold. That avoids overflow but changes the effective bias magnitude and could alter model behavior.
Liam: Proposal: triage -> add defensive guards -> tests -> staged rollout.
Jun: Root cause hypothesis: bf16 exponent overflow when slope * distance exceeds the representable BF16 range. ROPE-related rotation order might also worsen magnitudes in intermediate terms.
Ryan: Repro experiment: compute qk in native dtype, cast qk to FP32, compute alibi_fp32 and add; softmax in FP32. Maria, can you try that?
Maria: I tried the fp32-add flow: qk_fp32 = qk.to(torch.float32); alibi_fp32 = compute_alibi_fp32(); logits = qk_fp32 + alibi_fp32; softmax_fp32 = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1). That removes NaNs reliably.
Liam: Ok so mitigation paths: A) kernel change: always promote add+softmax to FP32 when dtype is BF16/FP16 and seq > threshold; B) short-term clamp bias; C) runtime kernel selection predicate to pick a "stable" attention kernel for risky combos.
Sophia: For selection predicate we can use: if dtype in (bf16, float16) and (uses_alibi or uses_rope) and seq_len > 2048 => use stable-attn (fp32-add + fp32-softmax).
Jun: Add microbench tests to ensure common short sequences don't regress more than ~10% in latency.
Ryan: Unit tests: fuzz seq lengths up to 8192, head dims at boundaries, both bf16/float16, assert no NaNs and L2 diff vs fp32 baseline within tolerance.
Liam: Operational plan: implement a canary flag in kernel-selector, enable on 10% of traffic for dedicated infra, monitor perf/cost, then ramp.
Maria: Implementation detail: minimize FP32 work: compute qk in native, promote qk to FP32 only for the add+softmax step. That keeps most compute in BF16. Also apply the standard softmax numeric trick (subtract max) to avoid exp overflow.
Sophia: I'll prototype slope-normalization to see if we can avoid FP32 path for some models; might be a cheaper fix for certain configs.
Liam: Add metadata to kernels so the selector/autotuner knows stable-attn has higher memory/compute and we can pick thresholds per GPU type.
Jun: Tests to add to CI: (1) golden snapshot for seed with seq=8192 BF16 ensuring no NaNs and L2 diff < 1e-2; (2) edge-case where slope*distance approaches overflow.
Ryan: I'll own the selector change and the rollout plan.
Maria: I'll add the repro to the repo and the new regression tests.
Liam: I'll draft a short RFC addendum documenting numeric guarantees and the selection predicate with perf numbers.
Sophia: I'll keep iterating on clamp/normalize prototypes; if we can avoid FP32 for many models that's ideal.

Maria: Thanks all. Please add a short note in eng-runtime/README about positional encoding numeric pitfalls so future kernel authors don't reintroduce this.
Liam: Will do. Marking triage complete for now; we'll regroup after the initial canary. :thumbsup:
